title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
blurb: Trained image and text encoders on 400 million image-caption pairs with a contrastive loss, producing a joint embedding space that classifies images zero-shot from class names.
intro: CLIP embeds a batch of images and their captions, normalises both, and trains so that each image's most similar caption in the batch is its own, and vice versa. The result is a pair of encoders whose cosine similarity measures image-text agreement. The steps build the ViT input embedding, masked pooling for text features, the symmetric contrastive loss and its sigmoid alternative, and retrieval; the capstone turns class names and prompt templates into a zero-shot classifier.
